esperance: Midday, camera slightly elevated at a three quarter angle over a wide brown river mouth in the Mekong delta. A small French steam gunboat lies across the river, blocking it: a short wooden hull with a copper-sheathed waterline, one black funnel with a thin trail of smoke, one small mast, a single cannon on the bow and a French tricolour flag (three vertical stripes blue, white, red) at the stern. About a dozen French sailors in white shirts and flat round caps on deck, one officer in a dark blue coat holding a telescope. Nipa palms and coconut palms line both banks, a few thatched stilt houses far off. The hull carries no name: no letters or numbers painted anywhere on the boat.
ghe-lua: Midday on the same wide brown river, camera slightly elevated at a three quarter angle. Five long wooden sampans loaded with heaps of rice sacks drift slowly in a line toward the viewer, each rowed by two or three Vietnamese men in dark ao ba ba with topknot hair and conical leaf hats, looking like ordinary rice traders. The tips of long spears are just visible, half hidden under straw mats along the sides of the boats. Far upstream, small in the distance, the French gunboat sits across the river. Nipa palms along both banks.
ntt: Medium shot on a sampan, daytime, camera at eye level. Nguyen Trung Truc, a Vietnamese man in his early twenties, stands at the stern of a wooden sampan holding a long oar, calm and determined, looking ahead. Dark brown ao ba ba, black hair tied in a topknot bun, a dark cloth scarf tied round his head. A fishing net and a woven basket lie in the boat. Behind him the river and a row of nipa palms. He is the clear subject, framed from the knees up and slightly off-centre, both hands on the oar.
danh-tau: Midday, camera slightly elevated at a three quarter angle. The sampans are pressed against the side of the French gunboat. Vietnamese fighters in dark ao ba ba with topknots leap from the sampans up onto the deck holding long spears and lit torches. French sailors in white shirts stumble back in surprise. One torch has set the canvas awning over the deck alight with small flat flames. Action without blood or wounds.
tau-chay: Wide view across the river from the near bank, daytime. The French gunboat explodes in the middle of the river: a big flat orange and yellow fireball bursts out of its hull, splintered wooden planks fly in arcs toward both banks, a tall column of grey smoke rises. Small sampans row away fast. Nipa palms on both banks. A few Vietnamese fighters on the near bank watch, seen from behind. No bodies, no blood.
don-kien-giang: Before dawn at 4 am, light blue-grey night tones that stay clearly readable. A small French colonial fort on flat delta land: earth ramparts topped by a wooden palisade, an open wooden gate, a wooden watchtower, a tricolour flag on a pole, a few low tiled barracks inside. About thirty Vietnamese fighters in dark ao ba ba with spears, machetes and torches pour through the open gate and climb the palisade on bamboo ladders. Small warm torch flames are the only warm colour. Camera slightly elevated at a three quarter angle. No blood.
phu-quoc: Daytime on Phu Quoc island, camera slightly elevated at a three quarter angle. A green forested hill rising straight from the sea. Nguyen Trung Truc and about ten tired fighters in dark ao ba ba stand among the trees on the hillside, looking down. Below them on the beach and in the bay, French marine infantry in dark blue jackets and white kepis with long muskets, and several small boats, encircle the foot of the hill. Blue sea, pale sky, a few palms on the beach.
phap-truong: Morning in the market square of Rach Gia in 1868, camera slightly elevated at a three quarter angle. Nguyen Trung Truc, a Vietnamese man of about thirty in a dark ao ba ba with a topknot, stands upright and calm in the middle of an open square, hands free and untied, no blindfold, head held high. A line of French marine infantry in dark blue jackets and white kepis with muskets at rest stands to one side with a French officer in a dark blue coat. A crowd of Vietnamese villagers in ao ba ba and conical hats watches silently from the edges of the square. Low thatched and tiled houses and coconut palms around the square. No weapon is raised, no executioner, no sword, no blood: only the quiet moment before.
co-nuoc-nam: Dawn over a Mekong delta riverbank, camera low near the ground. Tall wild grass fills the foreground and bends in the wind, a wide calm river behind it catching soft early light, nipa palms and a distant line of palm silhouettes on the far bank, one small empty sampan on the water. No people. Peaceful and a little melancholy.
